newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech SPT Telecom transfers E-mail unit.
newsitem.headline: Czech SPT Telecom transfers E-mail unit.

text.p: SPT Telecom, the Czech telephone monopoly, announced it would transfer control of its CZ-Mail data network service to the state natural gas distributor Transgas, an SPT spokesman said on Thursday.
"SPT Telecom and ... Transgas have agreed that Transgas would take over the CZ-Mail service, to date run by SPT Telecom," Evzen Stanek, SPT's spokesman said in a statement.
Terms of the deal were not disclosed.
He added the transfer would mean no break in services supplied to current CZ-Mail clients.

SPT said in March that it planned to end its operation of CZ-Mail and search for an organisation to take it over. Stanek said the best solution for continuing the service professionally was to sell it to Transgas.
Transgas has been running its own commercial data services within its more than 25-year-old telecommunication network used for operating its natural gas network, he said.
"Taking over CZ-Mail is in line with Transgas' plans to spread the offer of its data services," he added.
Transgas is one of the few companies that the Czech government has said it would not privatise.
SPT has been concentrating on doubling its fixed-line network during the 1990s.

In 1995, the government sold a 27 percent stake in SPT to a consortium comprising PTT Nederland NV and Swiss Telecom which promised to increase total connections to more than 400,000 by the end of the century from roughly 200,000 earlier in the decade.
